newsitem.title: CONGO: Sassou Nguesso says he backs Congo ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Sassou Nguesso says he backs Congo ceasefire.

text.p: Dissident Congolese militia leader Denis Sassou Nguesso called on his supporters on Wednesday to observe a ceasefire after seven days of fighting with the army of President Pascal Lissouba.
Sassou Nguesso, speaking on his militia's own radio station, asked "that the arms be silenced". He was responding to an earlier announcement by Lissouba of a unilateral ceasefire.

"I ask that the arms be silent and hope that other parties, at least this time, respect their commitments, and that the parties in conflict will keep their positions on the ground," the former Marxist president said.
Earlier in the day Lissouba had said on state radio: "I order an immediate ceasefire to give a chance for mediation. Peace must remain our first objective."

Lissouba's announcement followed a meeting he held on Tuesday with Brazzaville Mayor Bernard Kolelas who is chairing a mediation committee of the two sides. Kolelas was then due to hold a meeting on Wednesday with Sassou Nguesso to try to get his agreement to the ceasefire.
